summary: The Niche Pursuits host reviews four free calculator websites and estimates their traffic and display-ad revenue using third-party traffic data and assumed RPMs. The examples range from a simple bedtime calculator to a large general-purpose calculator site, with a seasonal snow-day predictor and a gematria tool in between. The host suggests calculator tools can work in narrow niches or be added to an existing website. The central lesson is that traffic and monetization matter as much as building the calculator, but the revenue figures are estimates rather than operator-verified results.

ideas.name: SleepCalculator.com
ideas.one_liner: A free bedtime calculator that uses a desired wake-up time to suggest when to go to bed.
ideas.business_model: Free calculator monetized with display advertising.
ideas.customer: People who want to plan their bedtime around a chosen wake-up time.
ideas.problem: Working out a bedtime and sleep-cycle timing can be inconvenient.
ideas.offer: Enter a wake-up time to get suggested bedtimes, possible wake-up times during the night, and an estimate of sleep cycles.

acquisition_channels.details: The host says the site gets organic visitors from Google and ranks for sleep-related searches such as sleep calculator and what time should I go to bed.

The host says the site has 1.63 million monthly visitors and 1.48 page views per visitor.

acquisition.how: Search traffic and repeat visits are inbound. Software can publish and monitor search-focused pages, with a person reviewing content and changes.

onboarding.how: A visitor can enter a wake-up time without a stated account or human onboarding process.

delivery.how: The bedtime and sleep-cycle results are produced by a simple calculation in the website.

billing.how: An ad network can serve ads and account for revenue; a person may still need to review payouts and records.

support.how: The simple calculator is likely to need little support, though errors or questions may still need occasional human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Wake-up and bedtime calculations apply equally in the UK; the site could localize language and advertising.

risks: The revenue estimate depends on third-party traffic estimates and an assumed RPM, not verified accounts from the operator.
The business depends on search rankings and ad demand, both of which can change.
